evidence: All seven acceptance criteria have named failing-capable selectors, negative-path coverage, production-path validation, real-checkout edge mutations, and a final full-suite run. One AC7 crash-recovery branch lacks an exact named selector.

findings.issue: AC7 requires fault injection before and after every prepare/fsync/CAS/reconcile seam, but its exact selector list names only a pre-CAS crash test; no selector explicitly proves the post-CAS state where the authority head exists while a derived projection is absent, global reads remain nonterminal, and reconciliation restores the exact immutable bytes.
findings.why: The atomicity strategy depends on this distinct recovery branch. The pre-CAS refusal and generic idempotent-replay selectors can both pass while post-CAS partial publication or reconciliation is broken, leaving the DoD claim at line 614 and the zero-partial-authority target at line 625 without failing-capable evidence.
findings.suggestion: Add a parameterized terminal fault-matrix selector covering before/after prepare, fsync, CAS, and reconcile; at minimum name a post-CAS test that removes one derived projection, asserts terminal reads and Done/merge/push/release remain blocked, runs reconcile, and verifies byte-identical restoration plus idempotent retry.
